title: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in Goats — Diagnosis and Control
content:
## Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in Goats

PPR is a highly contagious viral disease of goats and sheep. It is **notifiable** in Kenya and Tanzania. Mortality can reach 30–70% in unvaccinated herds.

### Symptoms

- High fever (40–41°C)
- Nasal and ocular discharge — thick, foul-smelling
- Difficulty breathing; coughing
- Lethargy, loss of appetite
- **Milk production drops sharply** in lactating does
- Diarrhea (sometimes bloody)
- Mouth lesions: erosions on gums, lips, and tongue
- Pneumonia in late stages

### Differential Diagnosis (lethargy + milk drop in goats)

| Cause | Distinguishing features |
|-------|------------------------|
| PPR | Fever, nasal/eye discharge, mouth lesions, herd spread |
| Internal parasites (Haemonchus) | Pale gums, bottle jaw, no fever, FAMACHA score high |
| Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia (CCPP) | Severe respiratory signs, no mouth lesions |
| Nutritional deficiency | Gradual decline, no fever, no discharge |
| Mastitis | Swollen udder, clots in milk, localized to affected does |

### Action Steps

1. **Isolate** affected animals immediately
2. **Call a veterinarian** — PPR is notifiable; lab confirmation via blood sample
3. Vaccinate all healthy animals in contact: PPR vaccine (live attenuated) — annual booster
4. Disinfect equipment and pens with 2% sodium hydroxide or iodine
5. Do NOT move animals to markets until 21 days after last case

### Prevention

- Annual PPR vaccination for all goats (kids from 3 months)
- Quarantine new animals for 21 days before introducing to herd
- Control ticks and improve ventilation in housing
content_sw:
## PPR (Peste des Petits Ruminants) kwa Mbuzi

PPR ni ugonjwa wa virusi unaosambaa haraka kwa mbuzi na kondoo.

### Dalili

- Homa, kutoka kamasi puani na macho
- Uchovu, kukataa kula
- **Uzalishaji wa maziwa unapungua** kwa mbuzi wa kunyonyesha
- Vidonda kinywani

### Hatua

1. Tenga waliougua mara moja
2. **Piga simu daktari wa mifugo** — PPR ni ugonjwa wa kutangazwa
3. Chanjo ya PPR kwa wote walio hai
4. Usafishe banda na vifaa

title: Internal Parasites (Worms) in Goats — Haemonchus and FAMACHA
content:
## Internal Parasites in Goats — Haemonchus contortus (Barber's Pole Worm)

The most common cause of lethargy and production loss in East African goats, especially during wet seasons.

### Symptoms

- Lethargy, weakness, reduced grazing
- **Pale inner eyelids (gums)** — anemia from blood-sucking worms
- Bottle jaw (fluid swelling under jaw) in severe cases
- Weight loss despite eating
- Reduced milk yield in lactating does
- Diarrhea in some cases

### Diagnosis

- **FAMACHA scoring:** Compare inner lower eyelid color to chart (1=red/healthy, 5=white/severe anemia)
- Treat only animals scoring 4–5 (selective treatment reduces resistance)
- Fecal egg count (FEC) via vet lab confirms worm burden

### Treatment

- Albendazole 7.5 mg/kg OR Ivermectin 0.2 mg/kg (rotate classes to prevent resistance)
- Iron supplement for severely anemic animals
- Re-check FAMACHA 14 days after treatment

### Prevention

- Rotational grazing; avoid overstocking
- Raise feeders — reduce fecal contamination of feed
- Selective deworming (FAMACHA) not blanket treatment
content_sw:
## Minyoo ya Ndani kwa Mbuzi

Minyoo (Haemonchus) ni sababu ya kawaida ya uchovu na kupungua kwa maziwa.

### Dalili

- Uchovu, kupungua uzito
- **Kope zilizopungua rangi** (damu kidogo)
- Kupungua kwa maziwa

### Tiba

- Albendazole au Ivermectin (kulingana na ushauri wa daktari wa mifugo)
- Tumia FAMACHA kuamua ni mbuzi gani watibiwe

title: Newcastle Disease in Chickens — Symptoms and Vaccination
content:
## Newcastle Disease (ND) in Chickens

Newcastle disease is the most devastating viral disease of village poultry in Africa. Mortality can reach 100% in unvaccinated flocks.

### Symptoms

- Respiratory signs: gasping, coughing, nasal discharge
- Nervous signs: twisted neck, circling, paralysis
- Green watery diarrhea
- Drop in egg production
- Sudden death without prior signs

### Vaccination Schedule (KALRO / FAO recommended)

- **Day 1–7:** Intraocular (eye drop) Hitchner B1 or LaSota strain
- **Day 21:** Booster LaSota (drinking water or spray)
- **Every 3 months:** Repeat LaSota booster for village flocks
- Buy vaccine from licensed agrovet; transport in cooler with ice pack

### Control During Outbreak

- Isolate sick birds; cull severely affected birds humanely
- Disinfect housing with Virkon or formalin (after removing birds)
- Do not introduce new birds for 30 days
- Report to local veterinary officer
content_sw:
## Ugonjwa wa Newcastle kwa Kuku

Ugonjwa wa virusi unaoua kuku wengi bila chanjo.

### Dalili

- Kukohoa, kupumua kwa shida
- Kuharisha kijani
- Kupungua kwa mayai

### Chanjo

- Siku 1–7: matone ya machoni
- Siku 21: chanjo ya ziada
- Kila miezi 3: chanjo ya kuendeleza

title: Bovine Mastitis — Milk Drop and Udder Health
content:
## Bovine Mastitis in Dairy Cows

Mastitis (udder infection) is the leading cause of milk quality loss and reduced yield in East African smallholder dairy.

### Symptoms

- Swollen, hot, painful udder quarter
- Clots, flakes, or blood in milk
- Reduced milk yield
- Cow may kick during milking; fever in acute cases
- Subclinical mastitis: no visible signs but milk fails CMT (California Mastitis Test)

### Treatment

- Identify affected quarter; milk out completely
- Intramammary antibiotic tubes (e.g. cloxacillin) — complete full course
- Withhold milk for withdrawal period stated on label
- Consult veterinarian for systemic antibiotics if cow is febrile

### Prevention

- Clean, dry bedding; milk in clean environment
- Post-milking teat dip (iodine or chlorhexidine)
- CMT test monthly to catch subclinical cases
- Dry cow therapy at end of lactation
content_sw:
## Mastitis kwa Ng'ombe wa Maziwa

Mastitis ni maambukizi ya chuchu yanayopunguza maziwa.

### Dalili

- Chuchu kuvimba na kuwa na uchungu
- Vipande kwenye maziwa
- Kupungua kwa maziwa

### Tiba na Kuzuia

- Dawa ya chuchu (kwa ushauri wa daktari wa mifugo)
- Weka chumvi ya teats baada ya kukamua
